properties.Name: Camp Lejeune Acquisition Boundary
properties.Description: The 110,000-acre land boundary acquired along the New River in 1941, evicting local farming and fishing communities.

properties.Name: Montford Point
properties.Description: Segregated training facility for the first African American recruits in the U.S. Marine Corps following Executive Order 8802.

properties.Name: Courthouse Bay
properties.Description: Historic agrarian and fishing landing repurposed into specialized amphibious water-training facilities for the base.

properties.Name: Jacksonville
properties.Description: A rural town that underwent rapid boomtown expansion and housing pressures right outside the newly constructed base gates.

properties.Name: Verona
properties.Description: Rail siding and rural junction heavily impacted by troop transport, heavy supply movement, and surrounding land condemnation.

properties.Name: Kellumtown (Hubert)
properties.Description: Historic African American rural settlement on the base periphery where displaced families sought post-eviction homes and land.

properties.Name: Sneads Ferry
properties.Description: Traditional coastal fishing community directly abutting the southern border of the Marine Corps amphibious training grounds.

properties.Name: Richlands
properties.Description: Inland farming community that absorbed displaced agricultural families moving northwest away from the base boundary.

properties.Name: Maysville
properties.Description: Northern gateway town along the rail line serving as a perimeter point for military transport heading toward New Bern.

properties.Name: Quantico
properties.Description: Virginia Marine Corps headquarters serving as the administrative authority and doctrine hub directing Camp Lejeune's expansion.
